subject: Availability calculation: maintenance vs. third-party outage (CL-20270819-03)
messages:
From: Cloudline Ops <ops@cloudline.net>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Availability question — CL-20270819-03

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking a look. We re-ran our post-incident reconciliation and still see a discrepancy between Cloudline's uptime ledger and the availability calculation Redwood provided for the 2027-08-19 window (incident CL-20270819-03). In our ledger we flagged a contiguous 41-minute degradation from 03:12–03:53 UTC. Redwood's response appears to have excluded the first 19 minutes as "upstream maintenance" and only counted a 22-minute degradation for our ledger.

We need clarification on two points:
- What exact maintenance window metadata was used to exclude the first 19 minutes? We have a maintenance entry on our side from 02:50–03:30 UTC for a peering cutover; we didn't expect that to eat into customer-facing availability.
- There's a third-party CDN failure that started at ~03:45 UTC and persisted for ~18 minutes. How are you attributing overlap between internal maintenance and downstream third-party outages when calculating credits?

Attached is our uptime_ledger.csv (timestamps in UTC) and the probe traces for the affected probes. Please loop in anyone on your side who handles SLA apportionment — this is blocking our internal billing reconciliation.

Regards,
Dawn Murray
SRE Manager, Cloudline Networks
Attachment: uptime_ledger.csv (CSV, 38 KB)

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: ops@cloudline.net
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability question — CL-20270819-03

Dawn — thanks for the ledger and probe traces, and sorry you're seeing the mismatch. I've pulled the initial calculations and want to be transparent about what we used so we can align.

Quick summary of what I see on our side:
- Redwood's incident timeline: 2027-08-19 02:58–03:55 UTC (rolling detection across edge clusters).
- We applied a maintenance exclusion tied to a scheduled kernel upgrade at 02:45–03:15 UTC that was annotated on our maintenance system as "kernel upgrade — infra team". The maintenance marker is per-cluster; for cluster-03 that you hit the maintenance ticket lists 02:45–03:15 UTC.
- The third-party CDN outage (reported by CDNVendor) began at ~03:45 UTC. For overlap periods our policy is to attribute time to third-party when the failure signature (response codes, traceroutes) points to an external hop failing — otherwise it's considered partial degradation of our service.

Before I draft a formal apportionment, can you confirm:
1) Whether your maintenance entry is referencing the same peering cutover (your ledger shows 02:50–03:30 UTC) or a different operation.
2) Which set of probe locations you used (we see probes from EU-west and US-east; attached traces only include EU-west).

I'm attaching a short prelim-timeline I generated from our logs so you can see the cluster-level annotations. Kim and Jonas — please see below, I think we should propose a clear split and a short statement of policy to avoid back-and-forth on credits.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachment: prelim-timeline.pdf (PDF, 92 KB)

From: Dawn Murray <dawn@cloudline.net>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Cloudline Legal <legal@cloudline.net>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability question — CL-20270819-03

Rishi — thanks for the quick reply and for sharing your timeline. A few clarifications from our side: we were performing a peering cutover on our edge (change ticket CL-PEER-719), not a kernel upgrade. The cutover was intended to be transparent; our engineers did not expect Redwood to classify that as "maintenance" that removes customer-facing availability time.

We can confirm the ledger timestamps (02:50–03:30 UTC) and we're attaching a second set of traces (US-east probes) that show failed TLS handshakes beginning ~03:44 UTC and clear traceroutes showing a CDN path failing at 03:46 UTC.

Given the overlap, Cloudline asks Redwood to:
- Reconsider the 19-minute maintenance exclusion and either provide the maintenance ticket id and owner (so we can validate the operational impact) or re-attribute the overlapping 02:58–03:12 window to Redwood's availability tally.
- If Redwood insists on the exclusion, produce a step-by-step apportionment showing exactly which minutes were removed and by what rule (maintenance metadata vs. probe attribution).

This is getting pulled into our billing/finance day cycle for August; we appreciate a concrete apportionment proposal we can review by EOD Monday.

Best,
Dawn Murray
SRE Manager, Cloudline Networks
Attachment: us-east-traces.zip (ZIP, 24 MB)

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: ops@cloudline.net
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 5 Sep 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability question — CL-20270819-03

Dawn — thanks for the extra traces and the ticket reference. I've reviewed the logs alongside Rishi's timeline and prepared a proposed apportionment for your review (attached). High level:

- 02:50–02:58 UTC (08 minutes): we agree this aligns with your peering cutover; Redwood considered this internal-to-Cloudline and we recommend treating it as Cloudline maintenance (no Redwood credit).
- 02:58–03:12 UTC (14 minutes): our edge cluster detected progressive request failures and HTTP 503s originating from our own upstream connection queues during the roll; because the signatures point to degraded CPU/kernel readiness on cluster-03 we propose attributing these 14 minutes to Redwood's partial degradation pool.
- 03:12–03:45 UTC (33 minutes): mixed-impact window where both the cutover and intermittent retries affected traffic — we propose a 50/50 split for these 33 minutes (16.5 min to Cloudline, 16.5 min to Redwood) in the ledger.
- 03:45–04:03 UTC (18 minutes): traced and confirmed as a third-party CDN outage; attribute to CDNVendor (no Redwood credit).

This yields a net Redwood-attributed availability hit of ~30.5 minutes. I've attached an apportionment-proposal.xlsx with minute-level breakdown and the supporting query IDs from our telemetry. If this is acceptable, we'll prepare a short statement we can both append to the billing reconciliation and I'll route the DocuSign link for the amended SLA credit agreement.

If you disagree with any specific minute-level attribution, call out the query IDs in the attachment and we'll re-open that slice for joint analysis. Our goal is a single reconciliation entry so your finance team can close August.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: apportionment-proposal.xlsx (XLSX, 48 KB)
